appraisal_events.evidence: la pensée de Swann se porta ... vers ce Vinteuil, vers ce frère inconnu et sublime ... l'audace d'un Vinteuil expérimentant, découvrant les lois secrètes d'une force inconnue ... Swann n'avait donc pas tort de croire que la phrase de la sonate existât réellement.
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann's meditation on the little phrase culminates in an extended, narrator-endorsed elevation of Vinteuil as a genius-creator comparable to great scientists, whose music attains a quasi-supernatural, immortal status.

appraisal_events.evidence: Swann comprit que le sentiment qu'Odette avait eu pour lui ne renaîtrait jamais, que ses espérances de bonheur ne se réaliseraient plus ... il songea que ... il aurait pu être obligé de quitter Odette ... on n'est jamais si heureux qu'on croit.
appraisal_events.explanation: After the concert Swann's hope of Odette's love ever returning collapses; the passage tracks his resignation to a permanently unhappy, dependent situation he lacks the courage to leave, closing on a bleak, self-doubting reflection.

status_effects.explanation: Vinteuil is locally elevated to the status of a sublime, almost superhuman artistic genius through Swann's admiring meditation, endorsed by the narrator.
Swann's remaining hope for a renewal of Odette's love is explicitly extinguished, and he recognizes himself as trapped in a hopeless, dependent situation he cannot bring himself to leave.
